Land at PVG.basis: PVG guides put full international arrival at ~60min; a domestic arrival (HO1148 from Guilin, T2) skips immigration, leaving deplane, long terminal walk and belt wait at ~35-45min.

Shanghai Maglev.basis: Operator and airport guides: 8-minute run PVG-Longyang Road with departures every 15-20min, so ticket, platform wait, ride and exit total roughly 25min.

Lunch.basis: China dining guides describe lunch (11:30-14:00) as the briskest of the three main meals; an unhurried tourist sit-down lands around an hour.

Check in at Marriott.basis: Standard city-hotel check-in plus bag drop and a quick freshen-up; no evidence of unusual delays at this property.

Nanjing Road East.basis: Guides say the full pedestrian street takes about two hours and 2-3h combined with the Bund; a one-way walk toward the river with browsing stops is about an hour.

The Bund.basis: GPSmyCity self-guided Bund route is 1.1km / about 1 hour, matching blog reports of 45-90min strolling the promenade.

Dinner.basis: China dining guides note dinner is the lingering meal (people 'spend a longer time at the table'), and Shanghai dinners commonly start 19:00-20:00; 90min covers a proper multi-dish meal.

Breakfast.basis: Standard hotel buffet breakfast pace; no venue-specific evidence, reasoned from typical unrushed hotel breakfasts.

Recovery massage / spa.basis: Shanghai spa listings (Time Out, SmartShanghai, Culture Trip) show 60-80min foot/body packages as the standard tourist option; add foot bath, changing and tea for ~90min door to door.

Jing’an Temple.basis: Multiple guides recommend about 1 hour for the compact walled complex (90min quoted as a generous middle ground); 45min is tight once you include ticketing and the Mahavira Hall.

Zhangyuan.basis: Reviews describe a restored shikumen retail precinct 'similar to Xintiandi but much quieter'; an unhurried wander of the lanes with a pop-up or two runs about an hour.

Nanjing Road West.basis: Shopping guides: most visitors spend 1-2h on West Nanjing Road, 2-3h if working through Plaza 66 / HKRI Taikoo Hui; 75min covers the strip plus one mall.

Dinner alt · Donghu Rd.basis: Same standard as a proper Shanghai sit-down dinner; Concession restaurant strips are relaxed rather than quick-turnover.

Wukang Building.basis: Walking guides treat Wukang Mansion as a photo landmark on the corner (best 16:00-17:30); it is exterior-only, so 15-25min including crowd jostling.

Wukang Road.basis: Guides quote 2-3h for Wukang Road with photos and coffee, but that bundles Ferguson Lane and cafes which are separate stops here; the 1.17km street alone walks in about an hour.

Ferguson Lane.basis: Ferguson Lane (376 Wukang Rd) is described as a small tucked-away courtyard of galleries and bistros — 15min to look, 45min if you actually sit for the coffee it exists for.

Anfu Road.basis: Wukang+Anfu combined walking routes are quoted at 3-4h over 2.5km; Anfu Road's own share, browsing a couple of shops, is roughly 45min.

Wulumuqi Road.basis: Guides frame Wulumuqi Middle Road as a short local-life detour (markets, Art Deco corner at Fuxing West Rd) rather than a destination; ~30min walk-through.

Sinan Mansions.basis: Travel guides advise 1-2h to walk the estate, admire the facades and browse boutiques/side galleries; 60min is the lower, unhurried-but-not-lingering end.

Fuxing Park.basis: Guides say Fuxing Park is 'worth a 30-60 minute walk'; 45min lets you watch the dancing and chess without circling twice.

Old Jazz Bar.basis: The Fairmont Peace Hotel Old Jazz Band plays a long nightly run (from ~18:30, sets through 23:30); reviewers describe staying for a couple of sets over drinks, roughly 90min.

Dinner alt · Fumin Rd.basis: Same standard as a proper Shanghai sit-down dinner; alternative Concession strip with comparable relaxed pace.

Yu Garden.basis: TripAdvisor/guide consensus is ~2h for a complete visit and 45-60min for a fast loop; at opening with fewer crowds, a highlights-plus circuit of the rockeries and pavilions is ~90min.

Yuyuan Bazaar.basis: Guides say you can 'easily spend an hour or two' in the bazaar alone (4h if you do garden, bazaar and dumpling houses together); 60min covers snacks and a souvenir sweep.

Mid-Lake Teahouse.basis: TripAdvisor reviewers report lingering 'an hour or two' over tea and the complimentary quail-egg/sweet snacks while watching the pond; 45min feels rushed for a set tea service.

City God Temple.basis: Guides quote 1-2h but that usually bundles the surrounding market; the walled temple itself (CNY10, 09:00-17:00) is compact and reads in ~45min.

People’s Square.basis: TripAdvisor reviews split between '10 minutes is plenty' for the plaza and 2-4h if you linger in People's Park; 45min suits its role here as a stroll-and-rest buffer.

M50 Creative Park.basis: Travel guides budget 2-4h (about 3h recommended) for 140+ studios and galleries plus the graffiti wall; 2h is a highlights-plus pass through the better galleries.

Huangpu night cruise.basis: Operators list the standard Shiliupu night cruise at 45-50min afloat; ticket redemption, security and boarding queues at the wharf add ~25min.

West Bund riverside.basis: No dedicated dwell figure found; the Xuhui riverside corridor linking the museums is a 10-15min walk each way, so ~45min allows an unhurried stroll with stops between venues.

West Bund Museum.basis: Museum lists 11:00-18:00 with last entry 17:00 across a modest number of galleries; guides recommend several hours only for major shows, so a highlights-plus visit is ~90min.

Long Museum West Bund.basis: TripAdvisor reviewers say 'about an hour to see it', some 'squeeze in two hours', and guides suggest 3-4h only for a blockbuster temporary show; 90min is the unhurried middle.

TANK Shanghai.basis: Some visitors suggest half a day, but TripAdvisor reviews repeatedly call the exhibits limited for the ticket price; the tanks plus the wrapping park read in about 75min.

Check in — J Hotel (Tower).basis: J Hotel's reception is on floor 101 of Shanghai Tower (check-in 15:00), so lift-lobby routing, the shuttle-lift ride and a luxury check-in run longer than a street-level desk.

Shanghai Tower base.basis: No published dwell time; the ground plaza and Exit 9A photo spot are the documented ground-level draws, and a walk around the base with photos is ~30min.

Jin Mao Tower.basis: Treated per the note as an exterior stop; going up would be different — the 88F deck is quoted at 2-3h and the Skywalk session alone is 45min plus 30min security check-in.

World Financial Center.basis: Exterior stop per the note; the 94/97/100F observatory would instead need 1-2h (30min on 94F, 20min on 97F, 1-1.5h on 100F) plus ticket and lift queues.

Shanghai Museum East.basis: Guides advise at least 2-3h and recommend 3-4h (3-5h thorough) for 20 halls; 3 focused hours covers the headline galleries plus one temporary show.

Pudong promenade.basis: Binjiang Avenue full route logs are 7.7km/2h, but the Lujiazui section fronting the towers is a fraction of that; TripAdvisor describes it as a short skyline stroll of ~45min.

Oriental Pearl Tower.basis: Exterior-only per the note, so a photo stop at the base; ascending instead runs 1-2h on the decks and 2-3h with the museum, plus 15-60min ticket and 10-60min lift queues.

Fly from PVG.basis: PVG guidance is to arrive 3h before an international departure (check-in closes 60min out), with Aug listed among the airport's busiest months; matches the note's 23:10 for a 02:10 flight.
